apparatus: 8-arm radial maze, 80 x 10 cm arms on an octagonal centre platform 24.7 cm across, and a rest box on the platform

sampling_rate.source: the Methods of Shipley et al. 2026 (PMC7619514): positions recorded 'at approximately 30Hz with some variability'; trialData.pos.header: sample_rate '30.0 hz'

position_span.source: the Methods of Shipley et al. 2026 (PMC7619514): '80cm x 10cm arms connected by an octagonal centre platform (24.7cm diameter, 10cm sides)', so arm end to arm end is 184.7 cm; the largest per-axis span of eight arms 45 degrees apart lies between 184.7 x cos(22.5 degrees) = 170.6 cm and 184.7 cm, and must lie within 20% of that range

speed_limit.source: Iriarte-Díaz 2002, J. Exp. Biol. 205:2897-2908, Table 1: Mus musculus runs at most 43.88 body lengths/s at a 0.080 m body length, 3.51 m/s (from Garland 1983 and Nowak 1999); times 1.5 because the tracked point is on the headstage, which swings faster than the body, and no source read states head speed

sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-04 against the files, the paper's Methods (Shipley et al. 2026, PMC7619514) and the record's MouseStats.xlsx. Files: the zip's MD5 is the one Figshare publishes (76eeedf2..., 4,364,634,689 bytes); its SHA-256 was computed from one full download, and each of the four members read is pinned by its own SHA-256 (equal to the survey's pins). Units: 71 clusters labelled 'good' in cluster_info.tsv; spike_times.npy / 30 kHz for them gives exactly the 1,201,058 curated spike times of trialData's 16 tetrodes. Time: trialData.pos holds 146,101 samples in 12 trials (0 to 10 and S2) and no sample times; the per-trial lines from pos_sample to spike time give 30.047 to 30.064 Hz with a largest residual of 41 ms. The camera's own timestamps in the zip's experiment_1_pos.npy files, checked for two trials, agree: trial 1 has 3,239 samples at 30.060 Hz (fit 30.060) and S2 81,278 samples at 30.050 Hz (fit 30.050), the same counts as trialData. Each trial starts 19 to 84 ms after the previous one ends; the spikes run from 0.04 to 4862.08 s. Space: pixels_per_metre 274 gives a range of 175.0 x 174.1 cm; the star placed on the maze trials' samples has arms at -152 to 162 degrees whose axes pass within 2.1 cm of one centre, and the samples reach 86.9 to 95.5 cm along the arms against the stated 92.35 cm. Heading: n_leds is 1 and pos.dir equals dir_disp in all samples. Genotype: m4005 is listed under AD in MouseStats.xlsx's Exp1Sessions. The overview figure (star over the path, the occupancy peak at the centre during rest) and three animation frames (Matplotlib backend) were looked at.
